title: How POS & Inventory Integration Could Work
disclaimer: Demo concept only — not a live POS recording. Simulated data.

scenes.title: Customer Orders
scenes.caption: A customer visits the website and orders products for pickup.
scenes.narration: A customer opens the Smoke and Supply website, browses the catalog, and places an order for in-store pickup.
scenes.visual: Storefront → catalog → cart → pickup checkout → confirmation

scenes.title: Order Reaches Store
scenes.caption: The website sends the order into an integration layer.
scenes.narration: Instead of stopping at the website, the order is handed to an integration layer that can talk to the store's existing systems.
scenes.visual: Flow: Customer → Website → Online Order → Integration Layer

scenes.title: POS
scenes.caption: The simulated POS receives the order.
scenes.narration: The point-of-sale system receives the online order so staff can prepare it alongside normal counter activity.
scenes.visual: Generic POS ticket mockup — no real vendor logos

scenes.title: Inventory
scenes.caption: Inventory updates automatically in the simulation.
scenes.narration: Inventory counts adjust when the online order is accepted, reducing the risk of showing items that are no longer available.

scenes.title: In-Store Sale
scenes.caption: A simulated in-store sale also reduces inventory.
scenes.narration: When a walk-in customer buys the same product at the counter, the POS inventory drops again.
scenes.visual: In-store sale chip; qty drops again

scenes.title: Website Updates
scenes.caption: After sync, the website reflects the updated inventory.
scenes.narration: A synchronization step copies the latest POS inventory back to the website so online shoppers see current availability.

scenes.title: Low Stock
scenes.caption: The system detects a product approaching its reorder threshold.
scenes.narration: When stock falls near the minimum threshold, the demo flags the product so the owner can review it.

scenes.title: Reorder Recommendation
scenes.caption: Current 8 · Minimum 10 · Velocity 4/day · Suggested 30
scenes.narration: For example, Product X shows eight units on hand, a minimum of ten, average daily sales of four, and a suggested reorder of thirty. Actual calculations would follow the store's business rules and supplier data.
scenes.visual: Reorder card with numbers; footnote demo formula

scenes.title: Owner Benefit
scenes.caption: One connected view of sales, stock, online orders, and reorders.
scenes.narration: The owner sees what is selling, what is running low, what customers are ordering online, what needs reordering, and how inventory is moving across online and in-store sales. One connected system can give the owner a clearer picture of inventory and sales.

endCard.headline: One connected system can give the owner a clearer picture of inventory and sales.
endCard.sub: This demonstration uses simulated data. Connecting a real store requires identifying the POS and inventory software first.
